title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the continuation (p. 696 bis/697) of the 'Longue Marche' notes. Grothendieck wants to relate certain homomorphisms, attached to the Galois action on the fundamental group of U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞} together with its S_3-symmetry, to the tower of Fermat curves over Q.

Setup (previous page). X_n : x_0^n + x_1^n + x_∞^n = 0 in P^2_Q, with U_n the open set where x_0 x_1 x_∞ ≠ 0. Acting on X_n are:
- the finite group scheme F_n^0 = μ_n^{0,1,∞}/μ_n (diagonal);
- the constant group S_3 = S_{0,1,∞}, by permuting coordinates;
- hence the semidirect product F_n = S_3 ⋉ F_n^0, a finite étale group scheme over S_0 = Spec Q.
The map (x_i) ↦ (x_i^n) identifies X_n/F_n^0 with X_1, which is the line x_0 + x_1 + x_∞ = 0, and U_1 ≅ U_{0,3}, S_3-equivariantly.

This page.
1. For n = n'd the map x_i ↦ x_i^d gives an exact sequence of group schemes (224): 1 → μ_d^{0,1,∞}(/μ_d) → F_n → F_{n'} → 1. It is the identity on S_3 (correcting the earlier 'g ↦ g^d') and the d-th power on the μ's. The d-th power map X_n → X_{n'} is compatible with (224) and induces an F_{n'}-equivariant isomorphism (225): X_{n'} ≅ X_n/(μ_d^{0,1,∞}/μ_d).
2. A crossed-out first attempt asserted that μ_n^{0,1,∞} acts freely on all of X_n. Grothendieck replaces it with the correct statement: F_n^0 acts freely on U_n. Hence U_n → U_{n'} is a torsor under F_d^0 = μ_d^{0,1,∞}/μ_d, and in particular U_n → U_{0,3} is an F_n^0 ≅ (Z/n)^2-torsor.
3. Passing to the limit (226): X_∞ = lim X_n, U_∞ = lim U_n, and F_∞ = lim F_n = S_3 ⋉ (Ẑ^{0,1,∞}/Ẑ) ⊗ T(G_m), with T(G_m) = Ẑ(1).

Next page. F_∞^0(Q̄) ≅ Ẑ(1)^3/Ẑ(1) is a Γ_Q-module via the cyclotomic character. U_∞ is a pro-torsor on which the 'S_3-equivariant arithmetic fundamental group' M_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3,Q}; S_3) acts compatibly.

In modern terms: the Fermat tower is the maximal abelian pro-cover of P^1 - {0,1,∞}. Its group is π_1^ab(U_{0,3,Q̄}) ≅ Ẑ(1)^{0,1,∞}/diagonal, i.e. H_1 generated by the three inertia loops subject to γ_0 γ_1 γ_∞ = 1. Grothendieck is setting up the Galois- and S_3-equivariant description of this abelian quotient of the arithmetic fundamental group of the stack [U_{0,3}/S_3].
errors: (224) is written once with kernel μ_d^{0,1,∞} and with F_n = S_3·μ_n^{0,1,∞}, without dividing by the diagonal μ_n. This is inconsistent with definition (221), where F_n^0 = μ_n^3/μ_n. With the quotient, the kernel is (μ_d^3·μ_n)/μ_n ≅ μ_d^3/μ_d, of order d^2, as in (225). The page writes it both ways.

The crossed-out claim that μ_n^{0,1,∞} (indeed even its quotient by the diagonal) acts freely on all of X_n is false: points with some x_i = 0 have nontrivial stabilizers. Grothendieck himself corrects this by restricting to U_n.
On the previous page 'g ↦ g^d' for g ∈ S_3 was wrong; here it is corrected to g ↦ g.
Minor: the limit is indexed by N* ordered by divisibility, which is implicit in the notation.

ideas.what: Fermat curves X_n as the S_3-equivariant tower of abelian (Z/n)^2-covers of P^1 - {0,1,∞} branched over 0, 1, ∞, with exact sequences of group schemes 1 → μ_d^3/μ_d → F_n → F_{n'} → 1
ideas.modern_name: Fermat tower as the maximal abelian (exponent-n) covers of the thrice-punctured line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weil on Jacobi sums 1952; Rohrlich 1977); systematized arithmetically by Ihara (1986) and Anderson (1987–89)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse d'un programme in this form; Longue Marche notes only

ideas.what: Limit F_∞ = S_3 ⋉ Ẑ(1)^{0,1,∞}/Ẑ(1) as the abelianized S_3-equivariant geometric fundamental group of U_{0,3}, with Γ_Q acting through the cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: π_1^ab of P^1 - {0,1,∞} (or of the stack [U_{0,3}/S_3]) as a Galois module
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Γ_Q acting on π_1 of U_{0,3} and the Teichmüller tower, but not this explicit Fermat-tower presentation

ideas.what: Plan to view U_∞ as a (F_∞^0, M_{0,3})-torsor, where M_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3,Q}; S_3) is an S_3-equivariant arithmetic fundamental group (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the abelian/Fermat quotient of the fundamental group of the orbifold [M_{0,4}/S_3]-type stack
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; Anderson–Ihara; Nakamura on S_3-symmetric versions

missed.claim: Around 1981, before Ihara's 1985–86 work on the Fermat tower and the pro-ℓ/metabelian Galois representation (the 'universal power series for Jacobi sums'), Grothendieck explicitly links the Galois action on π_1(U_{0,3}) with the Fermat tower, done S_3-equivariantly with group schemes over Q. This is a precursor of the Ihara/Anderson program. It goes no further than the abelian level on this page.
missed.quote: J'ai envie de mettre ces homomorphismes en relation avec la "tour" des courbes algébriques ... (courbe de Fermat d'indice n)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority/genealogy point: Grothendieck anticipated the use of the Fermat tower in anabelian Galois theory. The S_3-equivariant framing (working over the stack [U_{0,3}/S_3]) is less emphasized in Ihara's original treatment.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is routine: the Fermat curves form the abelian tower over P^1 - {0,1,∞}. Its interest is historical. It shows Grothendieck heading, circa 1981, toward the Fermat-tower/Jacobi-sum approach to Γ_Q acting on π_1(P^1 - {0,1,∞}) that Ihara and Anderson developed independently a few years later.
transcription_corrections: 'S_{3,S_0}' should be read as the constant group scheme 𝔖_3 over S_0 = Spec Q, written (𝔖_3)_{S_0}.
In (224) the image shows 'μ_d^{0,1,∞}' followed by a struck-out '/μ_d' (or overwritten μ_d) before the arrow to F_n.
On the next page the equation numbers '(277)' are '(227)'.
